iut_type: End Product (AlphaTheta DJ equipment, EP169), RF 2-item test Power Class discrepancy
customer_question: Our RF 2-item test came back classified as Power Class 2, but other products using the identical Bluetooth module have always tested as Class 1 — can you share the actual Output Power measurement values so we can investigate this discrepancy ourselves?
question_variants: Why did this product test as Class 2 when the same module tested Class 1 in other products?
Can you provide the raw Output Power figures for our own investigation?
actual_issue: The customer noticed an unexpected Power Class result inconsistent with their experience using the same Bluetooth module in other products, and proactively requested the underlying measurement data to investigate whether something was wrong with their hardware or with the test itself.
plain_english_explanation: Investigating the discrepancy revealed the Class 2 result was actually caused by a mistake in how Allion's own Test Plan was created for this engagement, not by any actual product issue — the measured output power was in fact within the overlapping range that both Class 1 and Class 2 cover, meaning the product would pass Class 1 testing without any problem once retested under a corrected Test Plan. The corrected Test Plan was prepared, and a subsequent retest using the appropriate Class 1 TX Power setting documented in the customer's own test-tool operation manual (matching a documented precedent from a similar past product, EP147, which also passed Class 1 at the specified output level) confirmed a Class 1 Pass.
consultant_answer: We found the issue: this was a mistake in how we created your Test Plan, not a problem with your product — your measured output power actually falls within the range that both Class 1 and Class 2 cover, so it will pass Class 1 testing without issue. We've corrected the Test Plan and will retest using the Class 1 TX Power setting documented in your own test-tool operation manual, consistent with how a similar past product (EP147) also passed Class 1 at that same output level.
decision_logic: When a Power Class result is unexpectedly inconsistent with prior experience using the same module, verify whether the Test Plan itself (rather than the product) is the source of the discrepancy before concluding a hardware issue exists, especially when the measured output falls within an overlapping range between classes.
final_recommendation: When a customer flags an unexpected Power Class result based on prior experience with the same module, transparently investigate and acknowledge any Test Plan creation errors found, and retest promptly using the corrected configuration rather than leaving the discrepancy unexplained.
risk_if_done_wrong: Failing to investigate and acknowledge a Test Plan creation error could leave the customer believing their product has a genuine hardware-level output deficiency, potentially triggering unnecessary hardware troubleshooting on their end.
